new_entities.name: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty
new_entities.description: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty and related palatal surgery intended to enlarge or stabilize the retropalatal airway in obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Obstructive sleep apnea severity
new_entities.description: Overall clinical or polysomnographic severity of obstructive sleep apnea, including event frequency and residual disease burden.

edges.effect_quant: Palatal surgery can improve OSA severity in selected patients, but effects are inconsistent. A 2025 meta-analysis of palatopharyngeal techniques found pooled AHI reduction of -5.2/h, while older UPPP cohorts showed only partial responder rates and long-term relapse.
edges.population: adults with retropalatal obstructive sleep apnea considered for palatal surgery, particularly selected surgical candidates
edges.mechanism: UPPP widens or stiffens the retropalatal airway and can reduce palatal collapse, but it does not correct multilevel obstruction and may leave clinically important residual disease.
edges.summary: This is not a cleanly protective edge. Some patients improve meaningfully, especially with favorable anatomy, but traditional UPPP is far from uniformly effective and long-term benefit can erode.
edges.caveats: Outcomes vary by surgical technique, baseline anatomy, and presence of hypopharyngeal collapse. Modern palatopharyngeal modifications may perform better than older cold-steel UPPP series, so historical results can understate newer technique-specific gains.

evidence.notes: Effectiveness of Palatopharyngeal Surgery Modifications in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Meta-analysis.

evidence.citation: KhanA et al 2009 Mayo Clin Proc
evidence.notes: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty in the management of obstructive sleep apnea: the mayo clinic experience.

effect_quant.comparator: Patients achieving at least 50% AHI reduction and-or postoperative AHI of 20 or less after UPPP

evidence.notes: Long-term results of uvulopalatopharyngoplasty for obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
